subject: Private deployment: trust anchor verification and DNS proofing for Acme Financial
messages:
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme-fin.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: security-qa@acme-fin.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 17:02:00 -0400
Subject: New private deploy - trust anchor + DNS proofing

Karthik,

Thanks for taking this. We are ramping an on-prem/private deployment of Redwood for a tranche of internal workloads that must not egress to public DNS or public CAs. Two asks to start the handoff:

1) We will provide our internal Root CA (PEM) and a short DNS proof (TXT) for the zone. We need guidance from Redwood on how to consume the root, how you expect split-horizon DNS to be configured, and what DNS records we must create for ephemeral hostnames the platform will request via ACME sidecar.

2) Audit/QA wants to confirm certificate lifecycle and rotation expectations: what lifetime we should request, how OCSP or stapling will be supported, and what logging you produce for private cert issuance.

Attached: acme-root-ca.pem (PEM), acme-dns-proof.txt (TXT with challenge).

Can we get a short checklist and a timeline? We prefer not to hold onto long-lived leaf keys in our environment; if Redwood's sidecar can mint short-lived certs against our root that would be ideal, but we need the threat model spelled out.

Thanks,
Sam Turner
Head of Platform – Acme Financial
sam.turner@acme-fin.com
(attachment: acme-root-ca.pem, type: PEM)
(attachment: acme-dns-proof.txt, type: text/plain)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme-fin.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com, ops@cloud-partner.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: New private deploy - trust anchor + DNS proofing

Sam —

Appreciate the files and the context. High level answer up front: we can support both (a) consuming your root CA in our Private control plane and issuing short-lived leaf certs via an ACME-style sidecar that uses your internal ACME endpoint, and (b) a brokered model where we return CSR bundles to you for signing. Each has different operational trade-offs (Redwood-managed key material vs customer-managed leaf keys).

To be concrete, here's a checklist we'll use to validate the setup and what we need from Acme: 

- Root CA ingestion: a PEM bundle for the root and any intermediates (you've sent the root; send intermediates if any).
- Zone delegation: the private zone or stub zone we will query. If you run split-horizon, please create an NS delegation for the subzone we will manage (e.g., _redwood.example.internal) or provide a conditional forwarder to your resolver.
- DNS proof: the attached TXT is fine. We'll validate by asking you to place a TXT at a specific name (we'll provide a unique token).
- ACME options: do you have an internal ACME server? If yes, provide the directory URL and any client auth method. If not, we will run a Redwood sidecar that acquires leaf certs by presenting a CSR to your KMS/HSM signing service; in that case we need an RPC API and service account.
- Leaf lifetime: recommended 6 hours to 7 days depending on sync capability; default for private is 24 hours. Tell us your max acceptable lifetime.
- OCSP/Stapling: For private CAs we prefer stapling at the edge. If your CA does not support OCSP, we will configure an internal CRL/OCSP mirror — please confirm that is acceptable.
- Audit logs: Redwood will emit issuance events to the private control plane and can ship signed issuance proofs to your S3/secure endpoint. Confirm the retention window required.

Action items for Acme to send back:
- Any intermediate certs.
- DNS admin contact and resolver details (IP CIDRs for conditional forwarder).
- Decision on ACME vs brokered signing and the maximum leaf TTL.
- Which team will hold the HSM/KMS access if you pick brokered signing.

I'll loop Laura (infra SRE) and Mina (release/ops) to take point on the implementation details. Proposed next step: 30-min sync tomorrow to align on delegation vs forwarder. Would 10:00am ET work?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-ephemeral-cert-policy.pdf, type: application/pdf)

From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme-fin.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: security-qa@acme-fin.com, ops@cloud-partner.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: New private deploy - trust anchor + DNS proofing

Karthik — thanks for the clear checklist. Answers inline below and attachments included:

- Intermediates: None, single-root PKI for now (attached).
- Zone: We'll create a stub-zone named redwood.acme.internal that forwards to our resolver pool at 10.10.20.0/24. Ops will open a ticket with neteng to add conditional forwarders by EOD.
- ACME: We do not run an ACME server. We do have an HSM-backed signing API (mTLS + client cert) that Ops can give a service account for.
- Leaf TTL: Security says maximum 72 hours for this class of workload. They prefer 24-hour certs.
- OCSP: Our CA publishes OCSP, but we will allow internal stapling if Redwood prefers.
- Audit: retention required = 3 years for issuance metadata, and signed proofs should be pushed weekly to our secure S3 bucket.

Attached: acme-root-ca.pem (again), acme-hsm-api-spec.pdf, dns-forwarder-plan.txt, acme-dns-proof.txt (contains token).

We can take the 10am ET slot tomorrow. Sam

(attachment: acme-hsm-api-spec.pdf, type: application/pdf)
(attachment: dns-forwarder-plan.txt, type: text/plain)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme-fin.com>, ops@cloud-partner.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: New private deploy - trust anchor verification and DNS proofing for Acme Financial

Thanks Sam — that's exactly the level of detail we need. Quick implementation notes and next steps so nothing falls through the cracks: 

1) Model chosen: brokered signing via Acme HSM API. Reason: your HSM gives you custody of private keys which satisfies compliance and auditors. Redwood will generate CSRs on behalf of workloads and POST them to your signing endpoint over mTLS.

2) DNS: we'll ask your DNS team to add the conditional forwarder for redwood.acme.internal to 10.10.20.0/24. For the initial validation token we will provide a random TXT name under _redwood-verify.redwood.acme.internal. Please place the token from acme-dns-proof.txt at that name; we'll validate during the provisioning window.

3) Cert lifetime and rotation: default 24h leaf certs, max 72h as you requested. Redwood will automatically rotate certificates and publish issuance events to the private control plane. We will enable stapling at the edge and, as a fallback, poll your OCSP responder every 5 minutes.

4) Audit/Retention: Redwood will sign weekly issuance snapshots and upload to your S3 path (please share the write role ARN). We will retain local issuance logs for 90 days; your requested 3-year retention will be fulfilled via S3 export.

5) Security checklist for tomorrow's sync (10:00am ET):
- Confirm mTLS client cert for Redwood service account and mTLS root for your HSM API.
- Confirm conditional forwarder configuration (exact resolver IPs).
- Test DNS TXT placement and provide confirmation.
- Exchange S3 export ARN and IAM role for uploads.

I'll record the meeting notes and open a short runbook in the secure-deploy-runbook link. Laura will draft the CSR/endpoint contract and Mina will own the rollout pin (canary -> 50% -> 100%).

See you tomorrow.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0199
